alalal-e90948-d1e101.summary: Rubric of the division of Lombard's text for Distinction 25, quoting its incipit on the sufficiency of faith.

alalal-e90948-d1e115.summary: Identifies this as the part treating faith in relation to believers.

alalal-e90948-d1e124.summary: Divides it in two: the state of faith across different times, and its equality in the believer with hope and charity ('Illud etiam non est praetermittendum').

alalal-e90948-d1e145.summary: Divides the first part into three: the faith of the Fathers; the faith of the simple ('Quid ergo dicetur de illis simplicibus'); and the faith of Cornelius ('Solet etiam quaeri de Cornelio').

alalal-e90948-d1e168.summary: Lists four doubts on the first part: whether faith can grow; whether it ever sufficed to believe that God exists and rewards those who seek him; whether faith can be subject to falsehood; and, since an article constrains belief, whether it constrains explicit or implicit belief.

alalal-e90948.summary: Division of Lombard's text for Distinction 25, which treats faith in relation to believers. Lombard considers the state of faith across times, covering the faith of the Fathers, of the simple and of Cornelius, and then the equality of faith with hope and charity in the believer. Albert raises four doubts on the first part: whether faith can grow; whether believing that God exists and rewards ever sufficed; whether faith can be subject to falsehood; and whether an article requires explicit or only implicit belief.
